text:
olga: quick sanity check — ran multitask QA sweep across 7b/13b at fp16/int8/int4 with different KV cache hit rates. need a short recommendation for product/GTN about which quant to route where and suggested rollout windows.

defon: tiny nit: devon :) can you paste the short numbers?

olga: oops typo, thanks. pasted below. tiny summary first: quality drop from fp16->int8 ~0.4 EM points on avg, int4 ~1.8 EM points; latency improvements p95 roughly 30-60% depending on seq len; cost per query down 2.8x (int8) and ~5x (int4) vs fp16 when batching. kv cache hit = huge multiplier on cost (1.6-2.2x saving at high hit).

maria: can we see the metric slices? long vs short, open-domain vs closed.

olga: yep, short table (multi-task aggregate across our 8 QA slices):
```
model | quant | EM | F1 | p95_ms | cost/query($)
13b fp16 | fp16 | 72.4 | 86.1 | 420 | 0.012
13b int8  | int8  | 72.0 | 85.9 | 340 | 0.0045
13b int4  | int4  | 70.6 | 84.8 | 260 | 0.0023
7b  fp16 | fp16 | 68.1 | 82.0 | 260 | 0.0065
7b  int4 | int4  | 66.9 | 80.8 | 200 | 0.0014
```

olga: kv-cache hit impact: with cold cache p95 + ~80ms and cost per query + ~30%. with 80% hit p95 drops by ~25% and cost/query goes down ~40% vs cold.

josh: thanks. EM drops look small for int8 but int4 starts to become nontrivial. do we have per-slice failure modes? hallucination/long-context recall?

olga: yes — int4 shows worse degradation on long-context multi-hop and on conversational coref tasks. single-turn extractive QA mostly fine.

kai: product ask: for GTN we need a simple rule: keep quality above baseline X, and cost under Y for self-serve. what's a crisp routing rule?

maria: propose: route short queries (<=128 tokens) to 7b int4 by default; medium (129-512) to 13b int8; long (>512) to 13b int8 fp16 fallback if fail detection triggers. set quality guardrail EM drop <=1.0 point vs hosted baseline for critical slices.

devon: +1 to that. add canary windows: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% over 48h with automated rollback if slice EM drop >1.5 or p95 regresses >20%.

josh: instrumentation: we need per-caller scorecard and synthetic probe traffic to evaluate drift. eval-bot: can you add those thresholds to the automated checks?

eval-bot: noted. creating checks: `slice_em_drop_threshold=1.5`, `p95_latency_regression=20%`, `kv_hit_monitoring=true`. will emit alerts to #eng-ml and create a GTN tag for rollback.

maria: also recommend an economic guard: if effective cost (post-kv) < 0.6x current fp16 cost and EM drop <=1.0 -> allow autopromote for self-serve. otherwise require SE review.

olga: suggested rollout doc blurb for GTN/product:
"Start with 7b-int4 for low-risk short-query buckets (<=128). For queries needing higher recall or >512 tokens, route to 13b-int8. Protect long-form multi-hop with a fp16 fallback that triggers if model confidence or reranker score drops below threshold. Canary at 0.5% for 4h, 2% for 20h, 10% for 48h. Automated rollback on slice EM drop >1.5 or p95 +20% or KV hit < 30% leading to cost > expected. Autopromote only when effective cost reduction >40% and avg EM drop <=1.0"

josh: where should the guardrails live? config flags in routing layer?

devon: yes — routing policy flags: `max_em_drop_per_slice`, `cost_threshold_efficiency`, `min_kv_hit`, `fallback_model` + time windows. we can plumb to console and have GTN UI show recommended policy.

kai: small ask for GTN: add a one-line “why this choice” for product (latency vs recall tradeoff) — they don't want to dig into tables.

maria: seconded. sample one-liner: "7b-int4 for short queries saves ~70% cost with <1pt EM loss; 13b-int8 preserves recall for complicated queries at ~30% cost reduction vs fp16."

olga: final practical note: run a 24h synthetic traffic run with representative KV hit distribution before the 0.5% canary to validate cost model. i'll schedule it.

josh: thanks — can you add the recommendation into the GTN handoff doc and tag me?

olga: will do. tagging @josh in the doc when ready. :thumbsup:

maria: LGTM, thanks.

devon: thanks all.

eval-bot: check completed: smoke probes scheduled for 24h; will post results under the doc thread.
